summary: Bob expands his drone observation of the native Deltans and studies their society through a virtual-reality reconstruction. He focuses on a young Deltan he calls Archimedes, whose solitary experiments produce handled stone tools and twine. New Bobs Marvin, Luke, and Bender come online to help; Marvin searches for flint while the group agrees to call the Deltans' world Eden.

updates.name: Deltans
updates.description: An intelligent, fire-using native people of Delta Eridani 4, named Deltans by Bob. They have bat- and pig-like faces, long spiderish limbs, brownish-gray to orangey-tan fur, patterned heads and mobile, expressive ears. They live in friendly tribes with two genders and loose pairings, and use clubs, rocks and pointed sticks as weapons.

updates.name: Eden
updates.description: The fourth inner rocky planet in the Delta Eridani system, also called Delta Eridani 4 and DE-4, and named Eden by Bob's group as the Deltans' birthplace. It is slightly larger than Earth, with lower gravity and a somewhat denser atmosphere. Its temperate-to-subtropical landscape mixes meadows, rocky bluffs and forests of huge brownish trees, and its varied wildlife includes six-legged insect and mammal analogues, bird analogues and a colour-changing winged creature Bob calls a hippogriff.

A practical drone design for planetary exploration. The football-sized surveillance variant carries cameras, microphones, gripping limbs and small reactors; the meter-long biological-analysis variant has many appendages and mechanical stomachs that analyze local organics in about a day. Both can change color with limited pattern mimicry. Surveillance drones can relay live video and record speech.

An automated factory used to gather and refine resources and to produce drones. It accepts designs made in virtual space and builds them with 3D printers, ROAMers, and nanites. Smaller units at material sites can make a few cargo drones at a time; larger units at Earth-Moon L4 and L5 are being set up to produce Bobs and drones and bootstrap industrial-scale equipment for colony ships. Its production priorities can be shifted from vessel assembly to computer cores. Standard templates include cradles that hold disembodied cores.
